column1: # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# Mechanical rewrites of the IEEE 1076-2019 package sources that make the derived
# packages of the older standards valid VHDL of their own standard
# (scripts/derive_ieee_packages.py).  Columns (tab separated): standard, package,
# files (decl, body or both), rule, item key (* = the whole file), arguments,
# clause, reason.  Rules: copy_as (the item becomes a copy of the item named by
# from= with the subst= identifiers old:new replaced), duplicate (a copy of the
# item with subst= follows it), substitute (identifiers replaced in the item or
# the whole file), drop_end_kind (the kind keyword after end is dropped),
# omit_file (the file is not shipped), insert_text (fsim-authored text= precedes
# the item; `\n` separates lines).  No rewrite adds text that is not a copy of
# 2019 text with identifiers replaced, except replace_text and insert_text rows,
# which each cite the older standard's clause.

column1: # READLINE and WRITELINE profiles of the older editions (checked against the editions' texts 11-19):
# 1076-1987 14.3 prints READLINE (F: in TEXT; L: out LINE) and WRITELINE (F: out TEXT; L in LINE); 1987 has
# no `file` interface class (4.3.3 interface declarations). The printed WRITELINE `L in LINE` lacks its
# colon and contradicts the same clause's prose (WRITELINE returns with L designating a null string, so L is
# updated): owner decision 11-19, L is inout as in 1993. 1076-1993 and 1076-2000 14.3 print READLINE with
# L: out LINE; 1076-2002 14.3 made it inout.

column8: VHDL-1987 READLINE takes F: in TEXT (no file interface class in 1987)
VHDL-1987 READLINE takes L: out LINE
VHDL-1987 WRITELINE takes F: out TEXT (no file interface class in 1987); L stays inout (owner 11-19: the printed `L in LINE` is a misprint, the prose updates L)
VHDL-1993 READLINE takes L: out LINE (IEEE Std 1076-2002 made it inout)
VHDL-2000 READLINE takes L: out LINE (IEEE Std 1076-2002 made it inout); applies over the 2002 rows to std/textio-2000.vhdl
